🚨Pulse Alpha is almost certainly a new model from Thinking Machines, and it's already available for free on OpenCode! I've been testing Pulse Alpha Free Max with the exact same prompt I used for Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, and it's been running for almost an hour now, while Opus finished in just 24 minutes and Astra took 32 minutes. Maybe it's taking longer because I'm using the highest reasoning setting, but from what I've seen so far, the quality is much better than I expected and I'm really liking the results!
I'm still running several more tests in parallel to see how it compares with other frontier models, so I'll have a lot more results to share soon. It's definitely slower in this particular benchmark, but the quality has been a really nice surprise so far, can't wait to see how the final result turns out!

items.title: Harness Engineering 2.0 is here!
items.summary:
Harness Engineering 2.0 is here!

We benchmark models all the time but the harness running the model can dramatically improve the result, cost, and execution time too.

And finally, devs just open-sourced Harness Arena, where you can test the same task across multiple harness and model combinations side by side.

You provide one task and then run it across several model x harness configs that you want to test.

Every config receives the same prompt, files, tools, skills, and evaluation checks. Harness Arena then returns:

- total cost
- execution time
- whether the task passed
- files and artifacts produced

If you want to try it yourself, it is implemented within the open-source HarnessRouter project.

Here's the repo: https://t.co/4y6zJShKSu

(don't forget to star it ⭐ )

HarnessRouter is a plug-and-play infrastructure layer that lets you run any harness under a single interface, like:

- Codex
- Hermes
- Claude code
- DeepSeek Harness
- System One, powered by Jev
- And 25 more agent harnesses

In Harness Arena, the cheapest run does not automatically win.

A config must complete the task correctly first. Cost and execution time are compared only among the configurations that pass.

Here's the result from one Harness Arena test:

- Hermes + GPT-5.2: 5/5 successful runs using 0.47 credits
- Claude Code + Opus 4.8: 3/5 successful runs using 223 credits

That is around 474x difference in credits, while the more expensive configuration also failed two runs.

You can keep the model fixed to measure how much the harness changes the result. Or vary both to find the best harness and model pairing for that task.

This helps answer practical questions such as:

- Should this task run on Codex or Claude?
- Can a cheaper config still pass every check?
- Which setup is best to handle this workload?

Once you find the best config, you can run future tasks through it using the same Unified Harness Protocol (UHP) interface for sessions, streaming, files, artifacts, cancellation, and failures.

So you are no longer choosing an agent stack based only on a model leaderboard.

Instead, you can benchmark the complete runtime on the task your product actually needs to solve.

To dive deeper, my co-founder wrote an article explaining why model routing is different from harness routing, how UHP works, and what supporting multiple agent runtimes involves.

It also covers the local setup, a working request, and how sessions and files move through the system.

Read it below.

If there’s even a slim chance that we’re losing control of the essential institutions that undergird society, he said, then we should focus on foiling that. But AI raises other questions too. What does it mean to be conscious? To create? To commune with other people? The answers are “entirely up for grabs,” he said. My anxiety’s still kicking around, but I [...] Some of the scenarios that people worry about—whether it’s biosecurity or a cyberattack or some of the everyday harms like the degradation of children’s social relationships—are very complex phenomena that can’t be easily tested or modeled by looking at a system in isolation. results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là hàm Python tính số Fibonacci bằng phương pháp đệ quy (recursion):

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    """Tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng đệ quy.

    Lưu ý: Cách này có độ phức tạp thời gian O(2^n) nên chỉ phù hợp
    cho các giá trị n nhỏ.
    """
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    else:
        return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)


# Ví dụ sử dụng:
# In ra 10 số Fibonacci đầu tiên
for i in range(10):
    print(f"F({i}) = {fibonacci(i)}")
```

### Giải thích:
- **Điều kiện dừng (Base case):** Nếu $n \le 0$ thì trả về `0`, nếu $n = 1$ thì trả về `1`. Đây là 2 giá trị cơ bản của dãy Fibonacci.
- **Bước đệ quy (Recursive step):** Với mọi $n > 1$, hàm sẽ gọi lại chính nó để tính tổng của 2 số liền trước là `fibonacci(n - 1)` và `fibonacci(n - 2)`.

*Lưu ý nhỏ:* Thuật toán đệ quy thuần túy này tính lại rất nhiều giá trị trùng lặp khi $n$ lớn, dẫn đến việc chạy chậm (tốn thời gian và dễ bị tràn bộ nhớ stack). Nếu bạn cần tính cho $n$ lớn (ví dụ $n > 30$), bạn nên dùng phương pháp **Memoization** (ghi nhớ kết quả đã tính) hoặc **lặp (iteration)**.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
